subject: Electrical Engineering
title: What Is a Signal?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Is a Signal?.

hook.text: A signal is any quantity that varies over time and carries information.

buildup.text: Sound waves, voltage waveforms, and radio broadcasts are all signals.

discovery.text: Signals can be continuous (analog) or discrete (digital). Both carry meaningful data.

twist.text: Noise is also a signal — but an unwanted one. Separating signal from noise is the core challenge.

climax.text: Signal processing extracts, cleans, and transforms information from raw measurements.

punchline.text: If it varies and carries meaning — it's a signal. Everything else is noise.

quiz.question: What distinguishes a signal from noise?
options: Signals are always louder than noise
A signal carries intended information; noise is unwanted interference
Noise is digital and signals are analog
